title: Continuatio Fragmentorum ex Adversariis mathematicis depromptorum

deep.reconstruction:
Problem (begun on p.506, item 106, noted as Krafft): square the alternating series s(a) = Σ_{k≥0} (-1)^k/(1+ka) and write s² as a manageable series.

Expanding s² and grouping the cross terms by the index difference m = k−j gives
s² = Σ_k 1/(1+ka)² + 2 Σ_{m≥1} (-1)^m S_m, where S_m = Σ_j 1/((1+ja)(1+(j+m)a)).
Partial fractions make S_m telescope: S_m = (1/(ma)) H_m(a), with H_m(a) = Σ_{i=0}^{m-1} 1/(1+ia). These are Euler's A, B, C on p.506–507.
So s² = Σ 1/(1+ka)² + z(1), where z(x) = Σ_{m≥1} (-1)^m (2/(ma)) H_m(a) xᵐ.

Evaluating z(1):
- Differentiate: dz/dx = Σ (-1)^m (2/a) H_m x^{m-1}.
- Multiply by (1+x). Since H_m − H_{m-1} = 1/(1+(m−1)a), the harmonic-type sums disappear: (1+x) z' = Σ_{k≥0} (-1)^{k+1} 2xᵏ/(a(1+ka)).
- Substitute x = yᵃ and multiply by y: (1+yᵃ) dz/(y^{a−2}dy) = −2 Σ (-1)ᵏ y^{ka+1}/(1+ka).
- Differentiating in y gives −2/(1+yᵃ). Hence z(y) = −2 ∫₀ʸ [u^{a−2}/(1+uᵃ)] F(u) du, with F(u) = ∫₀ᵘ dt/(1+tᵃ). Note that s = F(1).
- Final formula: s² = Σ 1/(1+ka)² − 2∫₀¹ [y^{a−2}/(1+yᵃ)] F(y) dy.

Case a = 2: the weight y⁰/(1+y²) equals F′(y), so the integral is a total derivative. Then z = −(arctan 1)² = −π²/16, and π²/16 = Σ 1/(2k+1)² − π²/16, i.e. Σ 1/(2k+1)² = π²/8. This is a self-contained derivation of the Basel sum (equivalent to ζ(2) = π²/6) from the Leibniz series.

Case a = 1: (log 2)² = ζ(2) − 2∫₀¹ log(1+y)/(y(1+y)) dy. Euler stops here without evaluating the integral.
errors: The double-series rearrangement (grouping s² by index differences) is not justified. The Cauchy product of an alternating series with itself is not guaranteed to converge, and conditionally convergent terms are reordered. The result is still correct: Σ(-1)^m H_m/m converges, and Abel's theorem as x→1 validates the generating-function step. Euler gives no justification.

In the a=1 case the final relation is left unevaluated. Since ∫₀¹ log(1+y)/(y(1+y)) dy = π²/12 − (log 2)²/2, it is a valid identity but circular as it stands: it is equivalent to ∫₀¹ log(1+y)/y dy = π²/12. Euler does not draw a conclusion from it.
Minor: the integration constants (lower limit 0) are implicit; they are correct because z(0)=0 and the bracket vanishes at y=0.

ideas.what: Square an alternating series, group cross terms by index difference, and telescope each group into (1/(ma)) times a partial harmonic-type sum
ideas.modern_name: Diagonal summation of a squared series; partial-fraction telescoping
ideas.where_published: Opera postuma (1862), this fragment; similar manipulations appear in Euler's work on series

ideas.what: Generating function of alternating harmonic-type sums, Σ(-1)^m H_m(a) xᵐ/m, evaluated through a first-order ODE: (1+x)z' removes the harmonic sums
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Euler sums, E477 'Meditationes circa singulare serierum genus', 1775/76); Nielsen in modern form
ideas.where_published: Related material in E477; this specific derivation only here (1862)

ideas.what: Proof of Σ1/(2k+1)² = π²/8 by squaring the Leibniz series: (π/4)² = Σ odd⁻² − (arctan 1)²
ideas.modern_name: A Basel-problem proof via the square of the Gregory–Leibniz series; equivalent to (arctan x)² = Σ(-1)^{n−1}(H_{2n} − ½H_n)x^{2n}/n
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler's published proofs are E41 (1735), E63 (1743, arcsin² integral) and others; squaring-Leibniz proofs also appear in modern recreational literature
ideas.where_published: Opera postuma I (1862), fragment 106 (Adversaria T.I pp.162–164)

ideas.what: General formula s(a)² = Σ(1+ka)⁻² − 2∫₀¹ y^{a−2}F(y)/(1+yᵃ) dy, with F the integral representation of s(a)
ideas.modern_name: Relation between squared Dirichlet-type series / Hurwitz-zeta values at 2 and iterated integrals (weight-2 polylogarithmic integrals)
ideas.where_published: only this fragment as far as known

ideas.what: a=1 case relating (log 2)², ζ(2) and ∫ log(1+y)/(y(1+y)) dy
ideas.modern_name: Alternating Euler sum Σ(-1)^{m+1}H_m/m = π²/12 − ½log²2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler sums in general to Euler (E477); this alternating value is classical (Nielsen and others)

missed.claim: In the a=1 case Euler stops at an unevaluated integral. Finishing it (∫₀¹ log(1+y)/y dy = π²/12) yields the alternating Euler sum Σ(-1)^{m+1}H_m/m = π²/12 − ½(log 2)². Together with the a=2 case, that would place an early alternating Euler-sum evaluation in the Adversaria, long before E477.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Dates Euler's contact with alternating double (Euler) sums and their iterated-integral representations earlier than his published work. Mainly of historical interest, since the identity itself is classical.

missed.claim: For general a the fragment gives an iterated-integral formula linking s(a)² to Σ1/(1+ka)², a Hurwitz-zeta value at 2. It closes in elementary terms only when y^{a−2} is proportional to F′, i.e. a=2. Pursuing other a (e.g. 3, 4) leads to weight-2 multiple-polylog (colored MZV) relations, which Euler did not explore here.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An early instance of the shuffle/stuffle-type comparison of a squared single sum with double sums. This is a known modern framework, so the novelty is historical rather than mathematical.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, lesser-known Euler derivation of π²/8 (hence ζ(2)) by squaring the Leibniz series via a generating function of alternating harmonic sums. It is published in Opera postuma, so it is in the record, but it is rarely cited among Euler's ζ(2) proofs. The a=1 case is left unfinished. The mathematics is otherwise classical.
transcription_corrections: No substantive errors found; the transcription matches the image. In the line for xdz/dx the image shows the terms aligned under the previous line (−2x/a·1, +2x²/a(1+1/(1+a)), −etc.), which the transcription reproduces.
